emp_engines.ponder.launcher.text_1: Fill a square with blocks of quartz. The ship will rest over it.
emp_engines.ponder.launcher.text_2: Surround it with a ring of brass casing, corners included
emp_engines.ponder.launcher.text_3: Stand a Resonance Pylon on top of each corner. The weakest pylon decides how long the run in the Etheric Skies lasts.
emp_engines.ponder.launcher.text_4: Place the Navigation Console on top of the ring. Right-click it for its screen: run length, weight limit, charge and destination.
emp_engines.ponder.launcher.text_5: Wrench a face of the ring to open that casing into a shaft input, then feed it rotation
emp_engines.ponder.launcher.text_6: Rotation charges the launcher: the pylons glow brighter and their rings spin faster. Heavier ships need more charge, and every input on the ring adds to the rate.
emp_engines.ponder.launcher.text_7: Bring a ship over the platform
emp_engines.ponder.launcher.text_8: When it is fully charged, a redstone signal starts the countdown
emp_engines.ponder.launcher.text_9: Beams of light land on the pylons, circle the ship until it's walled in light, and it's thrown up through the clouds into the Etheric Skies. The charge is spent, ready for the next launch.
block.emp_engines.obsidian_keyhole.locke: A hole seems to be in this block of obsidian. Maybe searching other portals would yield answers on the key.
block.emp_engines.obsidian_keyhole.fragm: The key is too broken to turn.
block.emp_engines.obsidian_keyhole.unloc: The key turns with a heavy click. The portal will light now.
item.emp_engines.obsidian_key.tooltip: Fits the keyhole in a nether portal's frame
item.emp_engines.navigational_data.toolt: Put it in a Navigation Console before launch: the ship arrives right next to it. Used up.
item.emp_engines.eye_mold_fragment.toolt: One of three pieces of an Ancient Eye Mold
message.emp_engines.sky_village_protecte: Sky villages can't be broken or built on.
